Exceptional Dental Care Experience in Bangkok

As an Austrian traveler who encountered an unexpected dental mishap, I found myself in a situation that could have easily derailed my journey.
While brushing my teeth, my front tooth crown just fell off at 3 am in the morning. What a nightmare!
At least i could recover the crown and i had 2 options - fly home and get the work done at my dentist or try it here.
I was very fortunate to find outstanding care at the Dental Hospital.

The next morning, thanks to the prompt and professional service at this clinic, my worries were swiftly put to rest.
Upon contacting the clinic, they demonstrated understanding the urgency of my situation, scheduling an appointment within the next hour.
Arriving at the clinic, I was friendly greeted by the ladies at the reception who had my information already available from previous visits (in the past I went there twice for routine dental cleaning). This was eliminating any unnecessary paperwork.

During my consultation, the dentist thoroughly assessed the situation, taking the time to listen to my concerns and explaining the treatment options available to me. His expertise and reassurance really gave me confidence that I was in capable hands and every aspect of my dental health was examined, including X-rays.
The dentist not only addressed the immediate issue of the fallen crown but also took the time to discuss preventive measures and options for ongoing care.

The clinic itself is also very impressive, with modern facilities spread across multiple levels, each dedicated to different aspects of dentistry. This setup gives me the confidence that whatever dental concern one might have, it could be addressed under one roof.

During my visit, I received not only the necessary treatment but also a complete dental cleaning. The professionalism by the dentist and the assisting personnel, was truly commendable.

What stood out the most was the genuine care and attention given to me as a foreigner in a foreign land. Despite the language barrier, the staff ensured clear communication, making me feel comfortable and well taken care of throughout the process.

The entire experience, from the initial consultation to the final result was exceptional. And to top it off, the pricing was fair and transparent, offering great value for the high-quality service received.

Also worth mentioning: Not only did they provide me with all the necessary X-rays via email for my records, but they also offered a complimentary shuttle service to and from the nearest BTS station, making transportation hassle-free, if necessary.

Of course I was lucky because my case was not the worst case scenario.
As someone with a long history of dental problems, i know that there are many cases where you will need more extensive treatments. And a dentist is not a magician who can fix all your dental problems in 3 hours.
But if you ever find yourself in need of dental care in Bangkok, I wholeheartedly recommend this clinic. Whether for emergencies or routine check-ups, you can trust that you'll be in the hands of skilled professionals .

Warning warning! Lying cheats! Don't ever go here, whatever you do. I went to this hospital for many years as it seemed to have a good reputation. Prior to this I'd never had any problems with my teeth (I am the son of a dentist, by the time I went here I was already in my late 30s without any dental issues and having had yearly check-ups my entire life). However, they immediately gave me 4 fillings on my 1st visit (which I've since learnt is a BIG warning sign of a scam dentist, but I was very trusting, I had never heard of lying scam dentists).

Over the years that followed they gave me another 5 fillings in the same 4 teeth. I could never work out how I could possibly have fillings as I take such good dental care of my teeth, I eat a healthy diet and floss daily etc (as you'd expect of a son of a dentist - I'd been told by my previous dentist that it's unlikely I would ever have any dental problems as my teeth were in such good condition). I'd ask the matronly old female dentist how it was possible I needed more fillings and each time she'd just say "care for your teeth better".

On my final visits, she told me I needed 2 fillings. Once again I was horrified that I could possibly have new problems with my teeth. I decided to have 1 filling that day and return 2 weeks later for the 2nd filling. When I returned 2 weeks later for the 2nd filling she told me that I needed 3 more fillings. She then said that I must have 'forgotten' what she'd said the previous visit. Seriously!? It was only then the penny dropped and I realized she was lying and making it all up. I felt like such a fool. I jumped out of the chair and left, thank god.

In the weeks that followed I went to 2 different new dentists. I didn't tell them anything of my history. I had full x-rays and check-ups just to be double sure. Both dentists told me there was no problems with my teeth, I didn't need 3 fillings, I didn't need any filings!

I'm so upset and feel like such an idiot. Not only have I wasted so much money on dental work I didn't need, my teeth are now ruined, they are so drilled that they have destroyed them and I'll likely need crowns on the teeth (perhaps this was their plan all along), which is going to cost a huge amount. I told my father and he said that he knows of many dentists who perform work when it isn't necessary. It's so sad this happens. And it happens here at this hospital. Whatever you do, DON'T GO HERE, they're liars, they'll perform unnecessary work on your teeth and even to the point of destroying your teeth so they can perform more work. Forewarned! I see they have some good reviews - perhaps for people with serious dental problems where they know they can make a buck they are able to help, but if you don't have problems with your teeth, I can tell you from my experience that they are happy to create nonexistent issues in order to charge you (regardless of how much damage they might do to your teeth).

POSTSCRIPT: As expected, the teeth that the elderly female dentist repeatedly drilled over and over again have now failed some time later and I've required crowns, costing many thousands of dollars. It's interesting to note that none of the crowns required root canals - as there had been no decay or infection on these teeth (she was just drilling the teeth to make money, and presumably, to damage the teeth to set up more work later). I'm so disappointed in myself for being so stupid as to believe this dentist/hospital when they were clearly lying all along, I'm a fool and I paid the price, but I hope this can serve as a warning to others, don't let them do anything to your teeth without getting an independent external second opinion from a more trustworthy dentist.

They wanted to work on 12 teeth replacing lots of old fillings and a root canal w/ a crown. I told them that I would think about it, and waited in the lobby for processing. I was not happy that they ended up charging me for them setting up for the root canal, despite not agreeing to it, and more than one xray fee because they somehow needed to xray my teeth more than once. I recently visited the dental hospital and overall, I had a good experience. The facilities were well-maintained, and the doctors and nurses were decent. However, there was one issue that I would like to highlight. The lack of floor signs inside the elevators was quite problematic.

When I entered the elevator, I found myself unsure of which floor to go to. I assumed that the first floor would be the reception area, but to my surprise, there was no one there. I decided to check the second floor, only to find out that it was dedicated to children department and the nurses there directed me to the 6th floor, where the main reception was located. I found it puzzling that a hospital, a place where clear directions are crucial, did not have any signs inside the elevators indicating the different floors.

When I mentioned this concern to the reception, they informed me that there were signs placed outside the elevators. While I understand their point, it would have been much easier for customers like me to know where to go if there were signs inside the elevator as well. People can often forget to read signs or may not notice them in the first place. In a public place such as a hospital, having signs inside the elevator is a common practice and helps customers navigate more easily.

Considering the limited space inside the elevator, I suggest that if putting signs for each floor seems too burdensome or cluttered, they could at least have a sign indicating that the main reception is located on the 6th floor. This way, customers would be aware of the specific floor they need to reach without overwhelming the elevator with multiple signs.

Unfortunately, the receptionists did not seem receptive to my suggestion. They did not show any willingness to address the issue or take the suggestion forward. They appeared certain that everyone should know that the reception area is located on the 6th floor. This lack of willingness to improve their services was disappointing, especially considering the reputation of this hospital.

Overall, I had a positive experience at the dental hospital in terms of the facilities, doctors, and nurses. However, I believe that the hospital's reception could benefit from additional training and should be more open to customer feedback. Implementing a sign inside the elevator, even if it's just for the 6th floor indicating the main reception, would greatly enhance the overall experience for patients and visitors, ensuring that they can easily find their way without unnecessary confusion.
